title: A Girl from a Small Village
text: Have you ever wondered if someone from a very small, remote village could grow up to lead thousands of people on a grand stage? Imagine a girl who dreamt of doing something different, something big!

title: What Do You Think?
text: If you wanted to join the defence forces like the Navy or Army, what kind of qualities do you think you would need? Would it be physical strength, courage, intelligence, or something else?

content.title: Life in the Indian Navy
content.description: The Indian Navy works on the sea. Ships are floating cities, and working on them requires teamwork, discipline, and constant learning. A doctor on a ship has to be ready for any medical emergency at sea.

title: Meet Lieutenant Commander Wahida Prism
text: Wahida Prism is a doctor in the Indian Navy. She comes from Thannamandi, a small village in Rajouri district, Jammu & Kashmir. She is the first woman to lead a passing out parade in the armed forces. Her father gave her the name 'Prism' because a prism reflects seven colours, just like the many talents he saw in her.

content.definition: A piece of glass that separates white light into a spectrum of seven colors. Wahida's father named her Prism hoping she would shine in many colors.
The military forces of a nation, including the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
A public march or gathering to celebrate or show military discipline. In a passing out parade, cadets officially become officers.

title: Reflect on Wahida's Journey
text: Wahida faced many difficulties. Girls in her village did not usually go to school or join the military. She had to study hard, ride a bicycle for miles, and join the Girl Guides. She proved that with determination, nothing is impossible. Think about a time when you found something difficult. How did you overcome it?

content.text: Encourage students to understand that the Armed Forces are not just for fighting, but also for providing medical help, rescue operations, and maintaining peace.

title: The Meaning of Discipline
text: During a parade, the leader has to give 36 commands in a loud and clear voice. If the leader makes even a small mistake, the entire parade can get ruined. This teaches us the importance of focus, discipline, and responsibility, which are useful not just in the military, but in every part of our lives, from school to sports.

content.text: Many people think that only men can join the military or lead parades. Wahida Prism's achievement shows that women are equally capable of leadership in the Armed Forces.

content.title: Be a Parade Commander!
content.text: Form a group with your friends. One person will be the Commander. The Commander will give instructions like 'Left Turn', 'Right Turn', and 'March Fast' in a loud, clear voice. See if the group can follow the commands perfectly without making any mistakes. Rotate the role of the Commander so everyone gets a chance to lead!
